impairmentSummary: The local 2026 303(d) county summary shows about 280.1 river miles in not supporting categories, 88.4 fully supporting miles, and 162.4 not assessed miles in Davidson County.
cejstSummary: Using the local Justice40 / CEJST tract snapshot, 64 of 161 census tracts in Davidson County are flagged as disadvantaged (39.8%). 0 tracts carry the water and wastewater stress flag, and 26 tracts carry the climate stress flag.

stressSummary.caveat: Water stressed and climate stressed are local labels for CEJST category flags. They are screening indicators, not direct measurements or regulatory determinations.

overview: Davidson County is represented as a Middle Tennessee county summary focused on urban river corridors, growth pressure, and environmental justice context. It intersects Lower Cumberland-Sycamore, Stones, Harpeth and overlaps 14 state legislative district labels plus 3 congressional district labels.
getInvolved: Review county and municipal agendas in Davidson County for stormwater, wastewater, landfill, quarry, and land-use decisions.
Use the county page to connect statewide indicators with local watersheds, monitoring stations, and source notes.
Check local monitoring and permit context alongside METRO WATER SERVICES; HARPETH VALLEY U.D. for community-specific follow-up.

indicators.label: Population
indicators.caveat: ACS estimates should be read as broad county context rather than precise local conditions.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by ACS county population, high to low.

indicators.label: Poverty rate
indicators.definition: Share of people below the poverty level based on ACS table B17001.
indicators.caveat: County-wide rates can hide tract-level variation.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by ACS county poverty rate, high to low.

indicators.label: Disadvantaged tracts
indicators.definition: Share of county tracts flagged as disadvantaged in the local Justice40 / CEJST tract snapshot.
indicators.caveat: Justice40 is a screening context, not a final judgment about community need.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by share of county tracts flagged as disadvantaged, high to low.

indicators.label: Impaired river miles
indicators.definition: Approximate river miles intersecting county boundaries in 2026 not supporting impairment categories.
indicators.caveat: Line segments are spatially intersected with county boundaries, so shared waters can contribute to multiple counties.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by impaired river miles, high to low.

indicators.label: Monitoring stations
indicators.definition: Distinct DWR water-quality monitoring stations associated with the county.
indicators.caveat: Station presence does not by itself indicate adequate monitoring coverage or condition.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by distinct monitoring stations, high to low.

indicators.label: Active water permits
indicators.definition: Count of active permitted features associated with the county in the local permit layer.
indicators.caveat: Permit counts mix facility types and do not directly measure pollutant load or compliance status.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by active permitted water features, high to low.

indicators.label: Scenic river miles
indicators.definition: Approximate miles of designated Tennessee scenic river segments intersecting the county.
indicators.caveat: This captures designated segments only, not broader watershed influence.

stateRank.basis: Ranked by designated scenic river miles, high to low.
